short: A crushing defeat for the Swedish-Protestant army that ended Swedish dominance in southern Germany.
full:
On 5–6 September 1634, a combined Swedish-Protestant army commanded by Gustaf Horn and Bernard of Saxe-Weimar confronted a unified Habsburg force composed of Imperial and Spanish troops. The Swedish commanders fundamentally underestimated the strength of their opponents, who had been heavily reinforced by a seasoned Spanish army marching from Italy.

The Protestant assault against entrenched Spanish positions on the Albuch hill resulted in disastrous casualties and a total rout. The Swedish army was effectively destroyed as an independent force in the south, Horn was captured, and the Heilbronn League of Protestant princes collapsed. The catastrophe forced France into direct, open participation in the war to prevent a complete Habsburg victory.
